problem.title: Design a Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection System (<30ms SLA)

spark.summary: Design a mission-critical Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection platform processing 50K payment authorizations/sec under a hard <30ms p99 SLA with zero single points of failure.
spark.keyTakeaway: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, execute Flink velocity updates, bounded Neo4j/TigerGraph 2-hop queries, and Triton XGBoost+GNN inference in parallel with strict per-hop timeouts.
spark.byteSummary:
Every credit card authorization waits synchronously on the fraud engine before returning an Approve or Decline to the merchant—if the fraud engine takes >30ms, checkout timeouts spike.

The architecture routes Payment Gateway events through Kafka into a Flink + RocksDB Velocity Aggregator while concurrently querying a sharded Neo4j/TigerGraph cluster for 2-hop device/card rings. Aggregated features hit an NVIDIA Triton Inference Server running XGBoost + GNN models.

The Decision Engine combines model scores with hot-reloadable compliance rules, while a Case Management & Chargeback Feedback Loop continuously updates entity blacklists and retrains models.

learningJourney.purpose: Allocate millisecond budgets across parallel feature enrichment and scoring.

explanation.foundation: Think of **30ms Latency Budget & Availability Targets** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection System (<30ms SLA): Allocate millisecond budgets across parallel feature enrichment and scoring.
explanation.core: At 50K TPS peak (Black Friday), the 30ms p99 budget breaks down into: 3ms Gateway + Auth, 10ms parallel Flink/RocksDB velocity + Graph 2-hop query, 8ms Triton XGBoost+GNN scoring, 4ms Decision Engine + Audit Log, and 5ms network buffer.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, 30ms latency budget & availability targets becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Mission-critical active-active fraud platform with Ed25519-signed DSL hot-reloads, 1M-tx dry-run simulation, and CRDT blacklist sync.

learningJourney.title: Synchronous Scoring & Async Feedback Topology
learningJourney.purpose: Separate the <30ms decision path from durable Kafka state and analyst feedback.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Synchronous Scoring & Async Feedback Topology** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection System (<30ms SLA): Separate the <30ms decision path from durable Kafka state and analyst feedback.
explanation.core: The Payment Gateway calls the Fraud Decision Service via gRPC while simultaneously publishing the event to Kafka. Flink maintains RocksDB velocity state, Triton scores the transaction, and every decision + analyst override loops back to update blacklists and training lakes.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, synchronous scoring & async feedback topology becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Mission-critical active-active fraud platform with Ed25519-signed DSL hot-reloads, 1M-tx dry-run simulation, and CRDT blacklist sync.

learningJourney.codeExample:
async def authorize_payment(tx):
    vel_task = asyncio.create_task(velocity_svc.get_and_inc(tx))
    graph_task = asyncio.create_task(graph_svc.query_2hop(tx.device_id))
    vel, graph = await asyncio.gather(vel_task, graph_task, return_exceptions=True)
    score = await triton_client.score(tx, vel, graph, timeout_ms=8)
    return decision_engine.evaluate(tx, score)

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection System (<30ms SLA) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, execute Flink velocity updates, bounded Neo4j/TigerGraph 2-hop queries, and Triton XGBoost+GNN inference in parallel with strict per-hop timeouts.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Idempotent Velocity Updates Under Retries
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent network retries from double-counting transaction velocity.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Idempotent Velocity Updates Under Retries** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection System (<30ms SLA): Prevent network retries from double-counting transaction velocity.
explanation.core: If a Payment Gateway retries a timed-out fraud check, naive velocity counters increment twice, falsely triggering a burst block. Keying updates by a 5-minute idempotency cache of tx_id in RocksDB guarantees each authorization is counted exactly once.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, idempotent velocity updates under retries becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Mission-critical active-active fraud platform with Ed25519-signed DSL hot-reloads, 1M-tx dry-run simulation, and CRDT blacklist sync.

learningJourney.title: Graph Partitioning & Asynchronous Edge Writes
learningJourney.purpose: Keep graph writes from blocking 2-hop read queries at 50K TPS.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Graph Partitioning & Asynchronous Edge Writes** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection System (<30ms SLA): Keep graph writes from blocking 2-hop read queries at 50K TPS.
explanation.core: Writing new Card->Device edges synchronously during checkout creates lock contention. We serve 2-hop reads from a read-optimized TigerGraph/Neo4j cluster and stream new edges asynchronously via Kafka with a 500ms micro-batch writer.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, graph partitioning & asynchronous edge writes becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Mission-critical active-active fraud platform with Ed25519-signed DSL hot-reloads, 1M-tx dry-run simulation, and CRDT blacklist sync.

learningJourney.title: Triton Ensemble Serving (XGBoost + GNN)
learningJourney.purpose: Run tabular GBDT and Graph Neural Network models together in <8ms.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Triton Ensemble Serving (XGBoost + GNN)** as the intuition layer for Design a Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection System (<30ms SLA): Run tabular GBDT and Graph Neural Network models together in <8ms.
explanation.core: NVIDIA Triton hosts both the FIL (Forest Inference Library) GPU-accelerated XGBoost model and a quantized PyTorch GNN encoder in a single DAG pipeline, eliminating inter-service serialization overhead and hitting <8ms p99.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, triton ensemble serving (xgboost + gnn) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Mission-critical active-active fraud platform with Ed25519-signed DSL hot-reloads, 1M-tx dry-run simulation, and CRDT blacklist sync.

options.feedback: Correct! Checking a 5-minute seen:tx_id key ensures retries return existing velocity without double-counting.

options.text: Disable all retries in the Payment Gateway
options.feedback: Disabling retries hurts payment success rates during transient network blips.

options.text: Run a 45-day Spark batch job on every retry
options.feedback: Spark cannot run inside a 30ms synchronous authorization.

options.feedback: Restarting Triton causes downtime and doesn't validate rule logic.

options.text: Dry-run the rule against 1M recent historical transactions to verify false-positive rate
options.feedback: Correct! Historical dry-run simulation catches overly broad rules before live enforcement.

options.text: Set the graph query timeout to 500ms

options.text: To fit both independent enrichments within a 10ms window inside the 30ms p99 SLA

options.text: Because Flink cannot read from Kafka if Neo4j is idle
To double the number of chargebacks

options.feedback: Triton receives one combined feature tensor.
